the intestinal microbiota of patients with CDI is characterized by increased abundance of Firmicutes, especially Lachnospiraceae, and decreased abundance of Proteobacteria, especially Enterobacteriaceae, compared with controls.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a novel biomarker of disease severity in patients with Clostridium Difficile Infection, which is a common cause of infectious diarrhea in hospitalized patients.
we have shown for the first time, to our knowledge, that a single fecal sample can be used to predict the severity of Clostridium (C.) difficile infection in a clinical population.
we can use a non-invasive, minimally invasive, and inexpensive method to detect the presence of bacteria in the gut.
